knowledge:
- key_parameters: model=Growth model, either exponential ("Exp" or "Bozic") or carrying capacity/logistic-like ("McFL") ;; keepEvery=Frequency of keeping population data; setting to NA prunes extinct clones and only returns existing ones at the end, significantly reducing memory and time ;; onlyCancer=If TRUE, simulations that end in extinction are repeated until the stopping/detection conditions are met ;; detectionProb=Stochastic stopping mechanism where detection probability increases with population size ;; checkSizePEvery=Interval between successive checks of the exiting condition; smaller values prevent massive population overshoots in fast-growing populations ;; muEF=Mutator effects specification ;; fixation=Genotypes that must fix to stop the simulation
- alternatives: Coalescent (backward-time) simulations=Much more efficient for simulating neutral data or simple selection scenarios ;; TTP (Java program)=Restricted to at most 4 drivers, no arbitrary CBNs/OTs/XORs, no passengers, single discrete-time model ;; FFPopSim=Another forward genetic simulator, but lacks OncoSimulR's unique order effects and "Lego system" for fitness specification ;; Special-purpose software=Preferable when fitness depends only on the total number of drivers and doesn't require complex epistatic/order tracking, as it runs much faster
- when_to_use: Appropriate for simulating asexual evolution (like cancer progression or bacterial/viral evolution under therapy) where fitness is a complex function of epistatic interactions, mutation order, frequency-dependent selection, or random fitness landscapes.
- pitfalls: Running exponential models with onlyCancer = TRUE and small initial sizes can cause many attempts due to frequent early extinctions ;; Using a large checkSizePEvery with fast-growing populations can lead to massive population overshoots and high iteration counts before the exit condition is checked ;; High mutation rates or keeping data too frequently (keepEvery = 1 instead of NA) can lead to huge memory consumption and slow execution due to tracking too many clones ;; The package fails some tests on aarch64 (arm64) platforms with macOS and is unsupported on that platform as of late 2024.

workflows.name: simulating_progression_with_dag_restrictions
workflows.intent: Specify fitness restrictions using a directed acyclic graph (DAG) or poset, simulate population growth, and sample the population.
input: data.frame (representing the DAG/poset restrictions with columns parent, child, s, sh, typeDep)
workflows.stages: 1. Specify fitness effects using allFitnessEffects with the restriction data frame ;; 2. Simulate individual trajectories using oncoSimulIndiv ;; 3. Sample the simulated population using samplePop
workflows.code:
pancr <- allFitnessEffects(
    data.frame(parent = c("Root", rep("KRAS", 4),
                   "SMAD4", "CDNK2A",
                   "TP53", "TP53", "MLL3"),
               child = c("KRAS","SMAD4", "CDNK2A",
                   "TP53", "MLL3",
                   rep("PXDN", 3), rep("TGFBR2", 2)),
               s = 0.1,
               sh = -0.9,
               typeDep = "MN"),
    drvNames = c("KRAS", "SMAD4", "CDNK2A", "TP53",
	             "MLL3", "TGFBR2", "PXDN"))
ep2 <- oncoSimulIndiv(pancr, model = "McFL",
                     mu = 1e-6,
                     sampleEvery = 0.02,
                     keepEvery = 1,
                     initSize = 1000,
                     finalTime = 20000,
                     detectionDrivers = 3,
                     onlyCancer = FALSE)

workflows.name: random_landscape_predictability
workflows.intent: Generate a random fitness landscape, simulate evolution on it, and calculate evolutionary predictability statistics.
workflows.stages: 1. Generate a random fitness landscape using rfitness ;; 2. Convert to fitness effects using allFitnessEffects with genotFitness ;; 3. Simulate population trajectories using oncoSimulPop with keepPhylog = TRUE ;; 4. Calculate predictability measures using LOD, POM, diversityLOD, and diversityPOM
workflows.code:
g <- 6
c <- runif(1, 1/5, 5)
rl <- rfitness(g, c = c, min_accessible_genotypes = g)
simulrl <- oncoSimulPop(10, allFitnessEffects(genotFitness = rl),
                        keepPhylog = TRUE, keepEvery = 1,
                        onlyCancer = TRUE,
                        initSize = 4000,
                        seed = NULL,
                        mc.cores = 2)
diversityLOD(LOD(simulrl))
diversityPOM(POM(simulrl))
sampledGenotypes(samplePop(simulrl, typeSample = "whole"))
